10.4Relations Do Not Form a Single Tree ​

In briefA tree showing only one hierarchy misses lateral or multiple relations; a multi-circle graph must retain relations of different directions, types, and times separately.

Actual multi-circle structures typically form a directed multigraph of relations with local containment. The same family can be nested within a community and within a legal system. A person can belong at the same time to overlapping family, work, platform, and interest circles. Platforms may bridge parallel groups. Different organizations can compete for funding, cooperate on safety, and overlap in personnel.

The framework therefore does not require each node to have only one parent node. Nor does “higher level” automatically mean greater importance, reality, or authority. Each edge expresses just one stated relation. If a pair of circles has multiple edges, the channel and time window for each edge should be recorded separately. If edges at different scales are incomparable, keep them side by side without forcing an order.

The graph representation must pass at least four checks. Has the analyst’s classification been mistaken for an object? Has a shared environment been mistaken for a direct relation? Has membership overlap been mistaken for organizational containment? Has contact with information been mistaken for effective feedback? Record feedback (§3.3) only when a signal returns and changes a subsequent state, transition probability, or constraint.

10.4Note

Understanding this section

10.4 Relations Are Not a Tree

A tree showing only one hierarchy misses lateral or multiple relations; a multi-circle graph must retain relations of different directions, types, and times separately.

The original’s key expression is ‘a directed multigraph of relations with local containment’. Directed means some edges have explicit sources and targets; multiple means one node pair may have several semantically different edges; local containment means one dimension may form a hierarchy without requiring the whole graph to be a tree. Symmetric overlap may be recorded as undirected semantics or paired edges; decorative arrows cannot create one-way effects. [T-main; T-rel]

Read this section’s family, community, and legal-system examples with §10.3.2: spatial belonging in a community differs from legal jurisdiction. A person’s family, work, platform, and interest identities should be recorded separately in actor–circle mapping Rac; one member referenced by multiple circles may then produce membership overlap in Rcc. Do not draw one person as several independent actors or automatically draw overlap as organizational subordination. [T-main; T-rel; T-joint]

Funding competition, safety cooperation, and personnel overlap may be three edges between the same organizations. Merging them into ‘close relations’ loses direction, windows, and mechanisms: funding competition may apply in one budget round, safety information may be shared long term, and a member may exit on a specific day. These edges can change independently; one failing does not erase the others. [T-main]

Vertical position in a graph confers no value or authority. ‘Higher level’ must refer back to specific containment, aggregation, or jurisdiction. Broader influence does not mean greater reality; larger organizations are not thereby entitled to decide for every member. Keep incomparable cross-scale edges side by side rather than inventing common weights for visual neatness. [T-main; T-scale]

Four graph checks ask whether nodes are merely unverified analyst categories, shared environments have been misdrawn as direct causes, shared members as organizational containment, or message contact as effective feedback. These constrain different errors. Supported node facts do not establish all edges; an edge’s existence does not establish causal effects; feedback requires return and subsequent change. [T-main; T-feedback]

Actual relation graphs may contain cycles, such as organizations messaging each other, without self-causation at one time. §11.7 later draws projected paths as time-unrolled directed acyclic graphs. Static relation structures and event paths have different semantics: acyclic path requirements cannot justify deleting actual return channels, nor can static circular arrows pretend to prove dynamic feedback. [T-path]

This section adds a graph-choice issue to NASA material: retaining only the Board’s organizational tree misses its working links and data support with MSC investigative teams. Adding such lateral interfaces preserves recorded relational facts without claiming improved predictive accuracy from a multilayer graph. For a narrow question of whom a team reports to, a local organizational tree may still suffice. [P-NASA; T-main; T-simple]

The strongest objection is that multiedge graphs are hard to read and measure. A reasonable simplification toggles relation layers by task rather than permanently merging them. Deduplicating personnel uses membership layers; asking about delay uses information and execution layers; asking about authority uses specific-matter layers. Unneeded layers may be hidden, but deleting source records and necessary distinctions cannot coexist with a claim to answer the original question completely. [T-simple]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    First establish separate object definitions for each node, preventing names from creating entities.

  2. 2

    Declare endpoints, type, direction, time, and evidence for each edge; permit multiple edges per node pair.

  3. 3

    Separate local containment, membership overlap, shared environments, and actual channels.

  4. 4

    Check the four misrepresentations, especially whether return actually changes subsequent states.

  5. 5

    Display a minimally sufficient subgraph for the task; neither complexity nor authority follows from graphics.

Distinctions to keep clear

Organizational tree

Can answer parent–child relations under a declared hierarchy.

≠

Multirelational graph

Allows lateral edges, different edge types, and local inclusion to coexist.

Static loop

Represents relations permitting travel in both directions.

≠

Effective feedback

Still requires temporal order, return, and subsequent change.

Rac

Membership-role relations from people to circles.

≠

Rcc

Relations between circles along specified dimensions.

Teaching construction: three edges between the same organizationsTeaching scenario

AssumptionsOrganizations, people, bench, and messages are artificial. Message edges indicate stipulated transmission without additionally assuming changed behavior.

Artificial organizations A and B each have a member set, sharing member c. One morning they compete for the sole laboratory bench while continually exchanging safety notices. Register separately a symmetric membership-overlap edge, morning resource-competition edges expressing mutual constraint, and A→B/B→A information edges. If c leaves B, delete only that intersection evidence, not automatically the safety interface. Adding another bench may eliminate morning competition while leaving overlap unchanged. Encoding overlap, competition, and safety information as 0/1 but retaining only their sum makes both (1,0,1) and (0,1,1) equal 2 despite requiring different updates. That summation cannot recover all three original fields. This limits a specified lossy sum, not every possible single-number encoding of structure.

BoundaryA counterexample about relational representation, not an estimate of actual organizational influence or a resource-allocation recommendation.

Working connections beyond Apollo 13's organizational treeDocumented case

The 1970 report lists the Board's group organization and also records coordination and data work between the Board and MSC investigation teams. A group-membership tree alone would lose the latter.

SourceReport of Apollo 13 Review BoardChapter 2, printed pp.2-1–2-2 and 2-17–2-18; PDF 32–33 and 48–49.Reading scope: Partly read

Scope and limitsIllustrates only that tree diagrams may omit recorded interfaces needed for a relational task. It claims neither unified organizational will nor support from grouping gain (§4.3).

Do two opposing arrows between organizations suffice to establish feedback?

No. Confirm that a prior state changes a subsequent state through a return channel; a drawn loop alone is insufficient.

Basis: Effective feedback (§3.3) and this section's fourth check.

After deleting the authority layer to simplify a graph, may it directly decide who can act?

No. It loses information necessary for an authority task; restore the specific authorization grounds.

Basis: Edges express only their declared relations.

Does requiring acyclic dynamic paths conflict with permitting loops in a relation graph?

No contradiction. Time-unfolded paths use new nodes for different rounds of a loop.

Basis: §11.7。

10.5Multiple Memberships and Role Conflicts ​

In brief“Who belongs where” is only a starting point. Knowing who can do what and bear which costs also requires recording entry, participation, exit, and authorization to represent others.

Membership cannot be reduced to a binary, permanent status. Records should include the basis for membership, start and end times, roles, strength of commitment, actual participation, ability to exit, and disputes. Formal members may lack the capability to act. Informal participants may bear key costs. People drawn in involuntarily may be unable to leave. Representatives may lack authorization from the people they represent.

Membership DimensionExample StatesImplication for Projection
Basis for entryVoluntary, employment, kinship, law, platform rules, shared exposure, or coercionDetermines the limits of responsibility and exit
Extent of participationCore, intermittent, peripheral, nominal, or passively bearing the consequencesDetermines visible information and channels of impact
RoleDecision-making, execution, care, bridging, oversight, affected party, or dissentDetermines rights, obligations, and conflicts
CommitmentHigh, medium, low, disputed, or unknownAffects paths without amounting to personality
Ability to exitFree, costly, subject to approval, or impossible in practiceTriggers the protection floor (§14.8) and the action ceiling

An actor’s multiple memberships do not automatically establish actual bridging. Potential bridging capability, actual transmission across boundaries, and outcomes caused by transmission are recorded separately. An identifiable interface supports a description of capability. Records of actual transmission support a description of the process. A causal effect on state requires a corresponding comparison. If recipients do not change their choices, this does not negate the limited transmission of information that already occurred. Authority to represent, transmission capability, and responsible parties must be kept distinct.

10.5Note

Understanding this section

10.5 Multiple memberships and role conflict

“Who belongs where” is only a starting point. Knowing who can do what and bear which costs also requires recording entry, participation, exit, and authorization to represent others.

The original states: “Membership cannot be reduced to a binary, permanent status.” A binary record may answer whether someone is on a list on a given date, but insufficiently explains actual action. Formal members may lack execution capability; unlisted people may bear key labor or losses. This calls for completing the definition of membership, not rejecting every explicit list. A reliable list can suffice for a narrow task. [T-main；T-simple]

The table distinguishes voluntary, employment, kinship, legal, platform-rule, shared-exposure, and forced entry. These suggest different responsibilities and exit conditions, not specific obligations inferable from identity labels alone. Legal duties require applicable-rule checks, employment requires contracts and actual circumstances. Common exposure means being drawn into effects, not consent to join. “Being in it” is not an authorization document. [T-main]

Participation ranging from core, intermittent, peripheral, and nominal to passively affected locates different positions of information and impact. Core personnel may see only part, while peripheral people may possess unique information. Roles further distinguish decision, execution, care, bridging, supervision, affectedness, and dissent. A core–periphery axis cannot replace these functions, nor can dissent automatically imply low commitment. [T-main]

Commitment may be high, medium, low, disputed, or unknown, but is a task- and time-conditioned record, not a personality grade. High commitment without time, resources, or rights does not establish action capability; unknown cannot be filled as low. Once actual participation is separated from expressed commitment, ask whether mismatches arise from resource limits, role conflict, risk, or material gaps rather than directly attributing motives. [T-main；T-M]

Exit capability distinguishes free exit, costly exit, approval-dependent exit, and practical inability to leave. It is not just a leave-group button: departure may cost income, care, identity, or safety. Inability to leave informs the protection floor and action ceiling, without authorizing researchers to decide for the person or imposing greater responsibility on those unable to exit. Distinguish exit protection from specific responsibilities that remain. [T-main；T-floor]

Multiple identities may create role conflict when simultaneous demands cannot both be met, or one role requires confidentiality and another disclosure. But multiple identities alone do not establish conflict. Identify specific matters, role requirements, deadlines, conflict mechanisms, and possible division of work or recusal. Two coexisting labels do not fill in hostility or dereliction. [T-main；T-rel]

The final paragraph separates cross-boundary connection into three levels. Identifiable interfaces support potential bridging capability; transmission records with recipients and times support process; changed choices or states require separate comparisons. Limited information transmission may genuinely occur even when recipients do not act. Representation also requires specific authorization, and responsibility requires the corresponding matter. Neither follows from “knows people on both sides.” [T-main；T-bridge]

Reusing NASA's report adds the observation that one person's posts cannot collapse into one camp label. The report lists Armstrong's Board, group-oversight, and MSC positions together, establishing only those listed positions. Separate organizational-coordination records cannot all be individually attributed to him, and dual positions cannot invent inner conflict. Historical material supplies both an example and an inferential boundary. [P-NASA]

The strongest objection is excessive cost and possible privacy intrusion from multidimensional person-by-person records. First select necessary items and windows according to the question, retain unknowns, and allow safe aggregation or the accounts of those concerned. A five-row table does not compel everyone to disclose their entire history. Simplification is acceptable if it preserves task-necessary exit, authorization, and harmed positions; if these are lost, the original question cannot be claimed completed. [T-main；T-M；T-simple]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Specify task, observation date, actor, and circle, first identifying which dimensions of membership are needed.

  2. 2

    Record entry basis, participation, role, commitment, and exit capability separately, plus start/end times and disputes.

  3. 3

    Look for incompatibility of specific requirements in matters or timing; multiple identities do not directly establish conflict.

  4. 4

    Separate bridging capability, transmission, and outcomes; check authorization and responsibility independently.

  5. 5

    Retain unknowns and protections for those unable to leave, using necessary, bearable material for bounded judgments.

Distinctions to keep clear

List status

Nominal or formal affiliation.

≠

Actual participation

What was done when and what was accessible; not automatically inferred from a list.

Commitment

Expressed intent, investment, or a grounded judgment concerning a matter.

≠

Personality

One commitment level cannot determine overall character.

Bridging

Interfaces and cross-boundary processes.

≠

Representative authority

Valid authorization by a specified subject for a specified matter.

Role conflict

Specific requirements have incompatible conditions.

≠

Multiple identities

Multiple memberships only; they may coexist peacefully.

Teaching construction: four hours and two role requirementsTeaching scenario

AssumptionsAll people, tasks, and deadlines are artificial. Work can be split by hour without quality changes, and permission is assumed in the counterfactual.

Within the same four-hour Tuesday window, A's role A requires 3 hours of nonparallelizable work and role B 2 hours. No delegation or postponement is allowed, so total demand 3+2=5 exceeds available 4, leaving a 1-hour gap. The conflict comes from the stipulated window and nonparallelizability, not A's two identities. If B can move 1 hour to Wednesday with permission, same-window demand falls to 4 and this temporal conflict disappears. Confidentiality or authority conflicts still require separate checking.

BoundaryA conditional calculation only, not a judgment of actual members' negligence, laziness, or susceptibility to forced overtime.

Teaching construction: a message arrives without changing plansTeaching scenario

AssumptionsSending, acknowledgment, prior information, and unchanged plans are stipulated. No actual communication was conducted.

A has explicit contacts in both circles A and B, sends a public meeting time to B's contact, and receives acknowledgment. B already knew the time, so plans do not change. The premise supports actual limited transmission but not an additional action effect. Without representative authorization, it also cannot establish that the sender committed circle A to anything.

BoundarySeparates process occurrence from causal increment, without claiming all information ineffective.

  1. 1

    May a caregiver lacking formal membership credentials be removed from analysis?

  2. 2

May a caregiver lacking formal membership credentials be removed from analysis?

Credentials alone cannot justify exclusion. If care is task-relevant, record actual role, cost, and entry basis.

Basis: Multidimensional membership records.

If A sends information to another circle, does that establish she represents the original circle?

No. Representative authorization for the specific matter requires separate checking.

Basis: Separate bridging, representative authority, and responsibility.

May a highly committed member who failed a task directly be judged dishonest?

No. First check capability, resources, time, conflicting requirements, and material gaps. Commitment is not a personality verdict.

Basis: The original separates commitment from actual participation.

Suppose two volunteer teams receive the same public warning on the same day. L is listed in both teams, but no cross-team transmission is recorded. May this be recorded as “one team transmitted information to the other”?

No. Both teams receiving the warning establishes only common exposure, recorded as shared environment. L's membership in both also does not establish actual bridging. Identifying a usable cross-team interface supports potential bridging capability; only actual transmission records allow this limited transmission to be recorded; any change in the other's arrangements requires corresponding comparisons.

Basis: Final paragraph of §10.5; see §10.3.1 for common exposure versus cross-circle propagation.

10.6Material Conditions and Experience–Meaning Conditions ​

In briefEquipment, money, and time tell us what can be done; experience, trust, and meaning tell us how circumstances are understood. They may interact, but neither can erase the other.

The joint state maintains both the material state (M) and the experience–meaning state (Ψ). The material state includes the body, time, space, money, energy, equipment, infrastructure, property rights, supply, care, and actual capability to act. The experience–meaning state includes feelings, expectations, memory, identity, trust, shame, hope, fear, commitments, conflicts of value, and perceived legitimacy.

The two channels can affect one another. For example, a platform’s rules for traffic change visibility and income, affecting material and informational conditions. Members interpret the decline as exclusion or failure, a change in experience and meaning. This interpretation may affect exit, protest, or cooperation and thereby feed back into platform metrics and resource allocation. Each step must specify a carrier, direction, delay, and counterexamples.

Bridge Between ChannelsStarting PointMediating FactorsOutcomeCounterfactual Question
Material→experience–meaningA change in income, space, the body, or timeSense of safety, sense of control, or interpretation of identityChanges in trust, fear, or commitmentDo interpretations differ under the same material change?
Experience–meaning→materialLegitimacy, hope, shame, or conflicts of valueCooperation, refusal, migration, care, or protestChanges in resource flows, labor, property rights, or use of facilitiesWould the action occur without the change in meaning?
Closed loop between the twoEffects in both directions occur in successionFeedback and tracesPath dependence or phase transitionDoes the return signal actually change a subsequent state?

Analyzing material and experience–meaning conditions side by side requires neither equal weights nor full collection on both sides for every narrow task. If the objective concerns members’ control, well-being, or relationships, relevant differences on both sides should be retained. For a question such as the total amount of equipment, for which an adequate summary is already available, the analysis may stop within that scope.

10.6Note

Understanding this section

10.6 Material conditions and experience–meaning conditions

Equipment, money, and time tell us what can be done; experience, trust, and meaning tell us how circumstances are understood. They may interact, but neither can erase the other.

The original requires that the joint state “maintains both the material state (M) and the experience–meaning state (Ψ).” M includes body, time, space, funds, energy, equipment, infrastructure, property rights, supply, care, and actual action capability. Ψ includes feelings, expectations, memory, identity, trust, shame, hope, fear, commitment, value conflicts, and perceived legitimacy. The former is more than money, the latter more than emotion and certainly not evidentially inaccessible “subjective noise.” Preserve task-relevant distinctions without demanding common units. [T-main]

The platform example first distinguishes how traffic-rule changes affect visibility and income, then how members interpret falling income, and only afterward whether interpretations change exit, protest, or cooperation. Establishing the first mechanism does not fill the next two. Some may interpret seasonal fluctuation; others may suspect exclusion. These experiences require material, not mind-reading from income curves. Feelings may be directly reported, while their external causes still require comparison. [T-main]

The table's M→Ψ bridge begins with resource, spatial, bodily, or temporal changes and reaches altered experience through perceived safety, control, or identity interpretation. The counterfactual question “Do interpretations differ under the same material change?” guards against treating material quantity as the sole sufficient cause, though observing differing interpretations does not itself isolate all confounding. The Ψ→M bridge requires meaning changes to alter resource flows, labor, property rights, or facility use through cooperation, refusal, migration, care, or protest. Attitude questionnaires without behavior and carriers cannot substantiate that bridge. [T-main]

A closed loop is not decorative double arrows. After M affects Ψ, evidence must show return changing subsequent M or constraints before it can be recorded as effective feedback (§3.3). Delays, directions, carriers, and counterexamples capable of cutting the chain require separation. Path dependence or phase conversion are candidate outcomes needing additional conditions, not inevitable results of correlation between the two sides. [T-main; T-feedback]

Proportionate treatment of both sides does not mean equal weights. Reliable quantity summaries may suffice for equipment inventories; questions about members' control, welfare, or relationships cannot be answered solely with resource totals if identical resources coexist with different actual control or dignity. Nor may all private experiences be demanded for “complete Ψ.” If material cannot be safely obtained, retain unknown or withheld-for-protection status and narrow conclusions, rather than recording missingness as nonexistence. [T-main; T-simple; T-floor]

The original Cash and Counseling report separately measures service use, satisfaction, and quality of life, suitably illustrating noninterchangeable endpoints. Its intervention combines the opportunity for an allowance, spending plans, counseling, and financial support. Reported group differences cannot be decomposed into pure cash effects or pure perceived-control effects. The observation used here is research design and endpoint separation, not proof of this framework or a causal M↔Ψ loop inferred from simultaneous improvement. [P-CC]

The next two subsections develop differences within M that also cannot be collapsed: §10.6.1 asks how resources become actual opportunities through institutions and positions; §10.6.2 asks how assets, cash, contracts, and financing transmit effects. They supply specific material-path mechanisms rather than reducing this section again to a single monetary indicator. [T-resource; T-finance]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Specify material and experiential-meaning endpoints and observation windows separately.

  2. 2

    For each bridge, list starting points, mediators, outcomes, carriers, directions, delays, and counterexamples.

  3. 3

    Distinguish personal reports, others' accounts, and analysts' interpretations; do not fill in one side directly from the other.

  4. 4

    Determine effective feedback only when return changes subsequent states; retain an unproved closed-loop candidate.

  5. 5

    Stop collection according to the task; when differences on both sides matter, totals cannot replace them.

Distinctions to keep clear

M

Available resources, conditions for action, and actual capabilities.

≠

Ψ

Experience, interpretation, commitments, and meaning; these cannot automatically follow from M.

Correlated change

Two quantities change together in observations.

≠

Cross-channel mechanism

Requires carriers, mediators, timing, and corresponding comparisons.

Proportionate treatment

Preserves differences genuinely needed by the task.

≠

Equal weighting

Presumes one half for each side; this section does not require it.

Teaching construction: two bridges that need not closeTeaching scenario

AssumptionsThe platform, counts, reports, and behavior are artificial assumptions; succession is not treated as causation.

Suppose an artificial platform changes A's visible opportunities from 10 to 6 per week. A reports unease but continues cooperating as usual, and platform metrics do not return any change. The assumptions support an M change and a Ψ report, not Ψ causing resource changes. If B interprets the same change as merely seasonal adjustment, the same material input permits different interpretations; these differences are not estimates of actual psychological effects.

BoundaryIllustrates evidential levels only, without judging actual users' motives or welfare.

Cash and Counseling: measuring services and experience separatelyDocumented case

The original 2005 report records random assignment of eligible volunteers in three states, followed by a nine-month survey of service use, unmet needs, satisfaction, and quality of life. Allowances came with spending plans, counseling, and financial support. Distinct endpoints and the combined intervention require separate interpretation.

SourceCarlson et al., Effect of Consumer Direction on Adults’ Personal Care and Well-Being in Arkansas, New Jersey and FloridaOriginal report, 2005-05-16; printed pp. 7–8, 12–14, 21, 45–48; PDF pp. 19–20, 24–26, 33, 57–60.Reading scope: Partly read

Scope and limitsSelf- or proxy-report surveys, differential exclusions, short follow-up, and voluntary enrollment limit generalization. Not all care was directly observed, nor were this section's bidirectional mediators identified.

Check your understanding

  1. 1

  2. 2

Can increased satisfaction directly replace records of service receipt?

No. They are different endpoints and should be measured separately.

Basis: The distinction between M and Ψ.

Does one project improving both use and satisfaction suffice to prove a closed loop?

No. Mediators, direction, return, and comparisons are still needed; a combined intervention also cannot be decomposed into single-component effects.

Basis: Cross-channel bridges in the table and effective feedback (§3.3).

Must an inventory question involve interviews about every employee's emotions?

No. If a sufficient inventory summary exists and the task does not concern experience, one may stop.

Basis: The original text's final paragraph.

10.6　物质条件与体验—意义条件; Chinese source lines 2285–2298; SHA-256 0d9e445bcba84380a572d248dad4836013b735d7d33589f29ea0c6f1aeb61c10

10.6.1Resource Conversion and Multiple Positions ​

In briefIdentical nominal resources need not yield identical available options. Trace the eligibility, timing, transport, care, and institutional rules through which resources become usable.

Resources create usable opportunities only under specific conditions for conversion. Income pays current expenses. Wealth provides a buffer or collateral. Qualifications and skills need recognition from the relevant institutions. Relationships must be possible to mobilize, and the other party must actually have resources and be willing to help. Transportation, time, care, standing under the law, information, and the cost of refusal may cause equal amounts of resources to yield different practical options. These quantities cannot be added into a single capital or power score without specifying units, conversion rules, double counting, weights, and purpose. A well-grounded monetary valuation or an index for a specific task can answer the question within its limits. A total cannot fill in each person’s control, qualifications, or well-being. A nominal allocation cannot substitute for resources actually at the recipient’s disposal.

The combined effects of multiple positions need not take the form of simple overlap among several circles. Rules of admission, accumulation of seniority, evaluation, and redress within the same institutional arrangement may change a group’s opportunities in succession. For example, later entry into a position where seniority accrues can continue to produce differences when opportunities are subsequently allocated uniformly by seniority. The sequence of rules, the denominators for entry at each stage, comparison groups, and positions that are absent should be traced. The number of categories, an interaction term, or a group average does not by itself establish the cause of harm to an individual.

Different statuses must not be put in a fixed order of disadvantage in advance. The same cue may receive different responses in different jobs, locations, relationships, or periods. Retain differences within categories, those who did not enter, and those who succeeded. Adding sensitive classifications is warranted only if it can answer a clear question, the material is sufficient to support it, and the privacy cost is tolerable. Do not compel disclosure to fill a cross-tabulation or treat the positions as nonexistent because the material cannot be obtained.

10.6.1Note

Understanding this section

10.6.1 Resource Conversion and Multiple Positions

Identical nominal resources need not yield identical available options. Trace the eligibility, timing, transport, care, and institutional rules through which resources become usable.

“Resources create usable opportunities only under specific conditions for conversion” separates resource amounts from feasible options. Income is a period flow that can pay current expenses; wealth is a point-in-time stock that may supply buffers or collateral. Wealth may also be illiquid or unavailable for disposal, qualifications and skills require recognition by relevant institutions, and contacts require others to be capable and willing to help. Having a contact or certificate cannot directly establish that something can be accomplished. [T-resource]

The original list—transport, time, care, legal status, information, and costs of refusal—seeks conversion conditions, not a preliminary vulnerability label for everyone. A free course incompatible with care duties, for example, remains infeasible despite a zero nominal price. Actual disposability depends on ownership, use restrictions, and execution conditions, not just an award notice. [T-resource]

Before adding different quantities, declare units, conversion rules, double counting, weights, and purposes. Income, assets, education, and contact counts cannot be added unqualified into capital or power. Evidenced monetary valuations or task-specific indices may be used, but totals do not supply personal control, eligibility, or welfare. An index's answerable scope comes from its original definition, not the grandeur of its name. [T-resource]

Multiple positions need not be intersections of several circles. One institution may first determine entry timing through admission rules, then rank accumulated seniority, distribute opportunities through uniform evaluation standards, and finally shape correction through remedy conditions. Each rule may look consistent in isolation while early entry differences propagate later. But sequences, denominators at every stage, comparison groups, and absent positions must be traced; endpoint gaps alone cannot identify one rule as the cause. [T-resource]

Category counts, one regression interaction term, or group means are not explanations of individual causes. Groups may contain different positions, periods, and support conditions; people outside the sample especially must not disappear. Additional sensitive classifications must answer an explicit question, have sufficient material support, and impose tolerable privacy costs. If a position cannot be safely observed, record the gap without compelled disclosure or treating the person as nonexistent. [T-resource; T-floor]

This section reuses Cash and Counseling with a new focus on procedural conversion from nominal eligibility to actual receipt. The original report describes spending plans and support processes and finds at nine months that only 39% of elderly treatment-group respondents still living in the community in Florida had recently received an allowance. Preserve that denominator and the “interview month or preceding month” window; it is not a statewide elderly receipt rate. Several candidate explanations exist for interstate differences; the proportion alone cannot identify a personality or single rule as their cause. [P-CC]

The strongest objection is that complete records of every conversion condition are difficult to achieve. Work backward from one key option to the most likely constraints, first testing low-cost modifiable items. If a total already sufficiently answers a bounded question, stop. But if the simplified question still asks about control or welfare, preserve conversion differences that change its answer. [T-resource; T-simple]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Begin with the actual option to be explained, distinguishing nominal from disposable resources.

  2. 2

    List units, timing, ownership, uses, and conversion conditions, preventing double counting.

  3. 3

    Trace institutional rule sequences and entry denominators at every stage, rather than comparing only those present at the endpoint.

  4. 4

    Use appropriate comparisons to judge mechanisms; averages or interaction terms do not automatically establish individual causation.

  5. 5

    Collect sensitive positions only according to necessity, safety, and material support.

Distinctions to keep clear

Benefit eligibility

May apply or have an opportunity to receive under program rules.

≠

Actually available

Funds, services, or opportunities are already disposable.

Multiple identities

One person occupies multiple classificatory positions.

≠

Rule sequence

Different stages of one institution successively generate conditional differences.

Task index

A summary with explicit definitions and uses.

≠

Individual welfare

Summary totals cannot recover every individual's feelings and control.

Teaching construction: nominal 100 and available 20Teaching scenario

AssumptionsAll amounts and arrangements are artificial, in the same currency and window, without duplicated costs; they represent no actual training or subsidy rules.

A and B each receive a one-time 100-yuan training subsidy. Suppose A has no associated costs, while B must first pay 40 yuan for transport and 40 for substitute care; the subsidy permits both uses and no other resources exist. Available course fees are respectively 100 and 100−40−40=20 yuan. A 50-yuan course is feasible for A but not B. An additional 40-yuan care subsidy gives B 60 yuan, crossing that price threshold.

BoundaryThe difference follows from the declared cost conditions, not a fixed identity-based vulnerability hierarchy or total welfare score.

Teaching construction: a sequence within one institutionTeaching scenario

AssumptionsTime is counted in complete years; eligibility is a necessary application condition, not a guarantee of promotion.

Positions A and B use the same promotion rule, “eligible to apply after two years.” Artificially set A's entry in 2020 and B's in 2021 due to earlier admission conditions. In 2022 A has two years while B does not. A uniform endpoint rule does not erase different starting points. Explaining B's later entry still requires checking admission grounds; years alone cannot establish discrimination.

BoundaryIllustrates sequential accumulation only, without validating any actual group's mechanism of disadvantage.

Cash and Counseling: the distance between eligibility and recent receiptDocumented case

Printed page 21 reports recent receipt by state and age. Among elderly treatment-group respondents still living in the community in Florida, 39% reported receiving an allowance in the interview month or preceding month at the nine-month interview. Spending plans and support processes are actual interfaces between eligibility and receipt.

SourceCarlson et al., Effect of Consumer Direction on Adults’ Personal Care and Well-Being in Arkansas, New Jersey and FloridaOriginal report, 2005-05-16; printed pp. 7–8, 12–14, 21, 45–48; PDF pp. 19–20, 24–26, 33, 57–60.Reading scope: Partly read

Scope and limitsThe 39% is not generalized statewide. One proportion cannot determine reasons for nonreceipt, interstate differences, or later welfare.

Check your understanding

  1. 1

    Can approval of 100 yuan be treated as receipt of 100 yuan's worth of services?

  2. 2

    Does a significant interaction term explain why a particular person lost an opportunity?

  3. 3

    Is requiring everyone to disclose sensitive identities for complete classification appropriate?

Can approval of 100 yuan be treated as receipt of 100 yuan's worth of services?

No. Receipt, uses, supply, and necessary costs still require checking.

Basis: Resource conversion.

Does a significant interaction term explain why a particular person lost an opportunity?

Not directly. Individual processes, baselines, comparisons, and other mechanisms still require material.

Basis: The distinction between group statistics and individual causes.

Is requiring everyone to disclose sensitive identities for complete classification appropriate?

No. An explicit task, supporting material, and tolerable privacy costs are required.

Basis: The original text's final paragraph.

10.6.2Assets, Liabilities, Contracts, and Transmission Through Credit ​

In briefHaving assets on paper, cash when payment is due, and access to further borrowing are three different things. Trace credit transmission through contracts step by step; co-movement of prices and spending does not itself identify an amplification mechanism.

In financial relations, the material state must at least distinguish stocks at a point in time from flows over a period, asset valuations from funds that can be converted into cash, principal payable from interest, and net worth from the ability to refinance. Assets in excess of liabilities do not guarantee that cash will be available when payments are due. A new loan does not by itself repair a shortfall in asset value. The market price of collateral, the contractual borrowing limit, the actual outstanding loan balance, and recovery on default are distinct quantities. Each must be tied to the currency, maturity, contract, repayment priority, and observation window.

One testable path of amplification starts with changes in assets or cash flow that alter net worth and the amount that can be pledged as collateral. Through loan quotes, credit limits, loan extensions, or margin calls, these changes affect net financing. Changes in financing then affect consumption, investment, hiring, and subsequent income and feed back into demand for assets. A candidate for self-reinforcement may be proposed only when the relevant constraints are binding and cash, equity, alternative loans, or arrangements for bearing risk have not cut the chain. Earnings expectations, interest rates, or policy may also drive prices and spending jointly. Changes in the same direction are insufficient to identify a financial accelerator mechanism.

In a financial network, common exposure, defaults on direct claims, calls on contractual guarantees, price spillovers from fire sales, and withdrawals of funds prompted by information must be recorded separately. Risk transfer changes who holds the risk and what they can bear. Whether it reduces overall risk still depends on the receiving party’s capital, contingent obligations, and who ultimately bears losses. The face values of mutual claims and liabilities across multiple layers must not be added up as net wealth for the system. Resumption of payments, restoration of capital, recovery of borrowers’ cash flow, and recovery of living conditions are different outcomes.

10.6.2Note

Understanding this section

10.6.2 Balance Sheets, Contracts, and Credit Transmission

Having assets on paper, cash when payment is due, and access to further borrowing are three different things. Trace credit transmission through contracts step by step; co-movement of prices and spending does not itself identify an amplification mechanism.

This section first separates measurement definitions: point-in-time stocks are assets or debt on a date, while period flows are income, expenditure, or net financing. Asset valuation is not immediately available cash, principal due is not interest, and net worth is not refinancing capacity. Assets minus liabilities yields meaningful net worth only in the same currency, under the same valuation basis, and on the same date. Positive net worth may still coexist with default due to insufficient cash at maturity; new borrowing increases both cash and liabilities without automatically repairing lost asset value. [T-finance]

Collateral market value, contractual lending limits, actual loan balances, and default recovery respectively address value, ceilings, usage, and recovery after default. Actual limits may depend on haircuts, priority, covenants, and lender judgments. Market value cannot all be treated as borrowable cash, nor loan balances as guaranteed recovery. Missing currency, maturity, contract, repayment priority, or observation-window information may change the comparison. [T-finance]

The candidate amplification chain runs from asset or cash-flow changes through net worth and pledgeable capacity to quotes, credit limits, extensions, or margin requirements, then to net financing, consumption, investment, employment, and subsequent income, returning to asset demand. Each arrow requires a carrier and delay. If constraints are not binding, cash, equity, or alternative loans remain available, or risk-bearing arrangements interrupt transmission, the same strength of self-reinforcement claim should not be retained. [T-finance]

Identifying financial acceleration requires excluding shared drivers. Profit expectations, interest rates, or policy may simultaneously move asset prices and spending; temporal order and positive correlation remain insufficient. Bernanke's 2007 personal review of research discusses both mechanisms and identification difficulties, including cash flow as a possible proxy for investment returns and alternative lending weakening bank transmission. This is a fact about historical research discussion; the speech does not establish that the mechanism caused any particular crisis. [P-FED; T-finance]

At the network level, five paths differ: common exposure means multiple parties hold the same risk source; direct-credit default is a contractual connection through debt nonpayment; guarantee calls activate contingent payment obligations; fire-sale price spillovers affect parties without direct lending ties through market prices; and information-induced withdrawals alter financing through beliefs and actions. These may coexist but cannot be drawn as one generic “contagion” edge that loses contracts, timing, and denominators. [T-finance]

Risk transfer changes the holder without necessarily reducing overall risk. Continue examining the recipient's capital, contingent obligations, and ultimate loss-bearing. Face values of reciprocal claims and debts within one system also cannot be added into system net wealth. Separate four final outcomes: restored payments, restored capital, restored borrower cash flow, and restored living conditions. Completing short-term payment does not mean an asset shortfall disappears, much less that life has recovered. [T-finance]

The strongest objection is that complex financial chains can become hindsight stories. Start with explicit contracts and a particular maturity window, testing which constraint actually binds. If constraints or return effects lack evidence, retain no-amplification or unknown results. The following are accounting teaching constructions only, not real borrowing, investment, or action recommendations. [T-finance]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Fix currency, time point, term, valuation, and contracts; separate stocks from flows.

  2. 2

    Calculate net worth, available cash, amounts due, and actual financing balances separately.

  3. 3

    Check step by step whether mediators such as credit limits, quotes, or extensions change and whether constraints bind.

  4. 4

    Distinguish five kinds of network transmission, comparing explanations such as shared expectations, interest rates, and policy.

  5. 5

    Evaluate payment, capital, income, and living outcomes separately; without evidence of a return, do not determine that there is self-reinforcement.

Distinctions to keep clear

Net worth

Assets minus liabilities on the same date.

≠

Liquidity

Whether cash for payment can be obtained in time for the specified horizon.

Credit limit

The contractually permitted borrowing ceiling.

≠

Balance

Actual outstanding borrowing, which need not equal the limit.

Risk transfer

Risk changes holder.

≠

Risk reduction

Requires examining the entire system and ultimate loss-bearing.

Mathematical teaching construction: positive net worth with a payment shortfallTeaching scenario

AssumptionsEntirely constructed, using one currency, without interest, fees, or valuation changes. Borrowing is genuinely approved and received; equipment cannot be liquidated before tomorrow.

On the same date, a constructed entity holds cash of 5 yuan, equipment worth 95 that cannot be liquidated by tomorrow, and liabilities of 80, of which 20 falls due tomorrow. Net worth=(5+95)−80=20 yuan, but tomorrow's cash shortfall=20−5=15 yuan. Borrowing 15 raises cash to 20 and liabilities to 95, leaving net worth=(20+95)−95=20 yuan. Repaying 20 of old debt leaves cash 0, equipment 95, and liabilities 75, still net worth 20 yuan. New borrowing fills the cash shortfall for a specified horizon without creating net worth.

BoundaryAn accounting identity does not establish that real refinancing is feasible or can continue indefinitely.

Mathematical teaching construction: credit limit and balanceTeaching scenario

AssumptionsA constructed contract with a fixed ratio and one valuation update; market value, credit limit, and balance must not be conflated.

Collateral has market value 100 yuan and the contract permits a maximum loan-to-value ratio of 60%, so the credit limit is 60 yuan. An outstanding balance of 50 leaves 10 unused. If market value becomes 80 and contractual revaluation takes effect immediately, the limit becomes 48 while the balance remains 50, a shortfall of 2. Immediate top-up pressure arises only if the contract actually requires it and provides no grace period or substitute collateral. If the borrower has another 2 yuan in cash, the shortfall can be met without a forced sale.

BoundaryNo subsequent asset-price feedback has been established; the 2-yuan shortfall cannot directly be called systemic financial acceleration.

Researchers' 2007 qualifications on identifying financial accelerationDocumented case

In his June 15, 2007 speech, Bernanke explains the external-finance-premium mechanism while noting that cash flow may proxy difficult-to-measure investment returns. His discussion of bank transmission also requires borrowers to be unable to switch costlessly to other sources.

10.7Five Kinds of Clock and Asynchronous Updating ​

In briefEvents on the same day do not update every state simultaneously. Distinguish what an event reaches, how a process advances on its own, and when a change is actually observed.

A joint state needs to distinguish at least five kinds of clock: immediate, interactive, organizational, institutional, and long-term. Immediate reactions may be measured in minutes, trust in interaction in rounds, organizational budgets in quarters, institutional write-back in deliberation cycles, and long-term learning or generational change in years. The timing of the same event’s effects varies by variable.

ClockTypical ObjectsUpdate TriggerCommon Error
ImmediateEmotion, attention, bodily arousal, local pricesArrival of a signal or a direct shockRecording short-term fluctuations as long-term change
InteractiveTrust, strategies, expectations in relationships, local normsSeveral rounds of action and feedbackIgnoring the order of rounds and memory
OrganizationalRoles, budgets, processes, metricsCycles of decision, execution, and reviewAssuming a decision amounts to implementation
InstitutionalRules, rights, responsibilities, appeals, recordsActual change in rules or procedures, actual write-back, and execution. Record authorization and legal validity separatelyTreating a verbal commitment as institutional change
Long-termCapabilities, identity, infrastructure, culture, and relations across generationsAccumulation, learning, maintenance, and replacementExtrapolating to the long term from short-term data

External events directly update only variables reached through their channels and for which the conditions hold. Endogenous processes, expiration, accumulation, and recovery proceed on their own clocks and under the stated rules for dynamics. A variable untouched by the current event is not necessarily unchanged in reality. Without reliable grounds for an update, retain the last observed value, its time, and uncertainty, or mark it “unknown.” Do not refresh all variables at once just to make the joint snapshot “complete.”

Asynchrony can also change the direction of effects. Asset prices can change immediately, while loan contracts adjust only upon revaluation or renewal. The timing of payments differs between fixed-rate and floating-rate debt. Public guarantees may provide cash first and distribute losses later. A joint projection should check when each constraint actually binds, when alternative financing is possible, and whether the recovery window precedes irreversible harm. Extending a short-term backstop must not be treated as restoration of the long-term ability to repay.

10.7Note

Understanding this section

10.7 Five clock types and asynchronous updating

Events on the same day do not update every state simultaneously. Distinguish what an event reaches, how a process advances on its own, and when a change is actually observed.

The source distinguishes at least five clock types: immediate, interactional, organizational, institutional, and long-term. They are analytical categories for recognizing updating mechanisms, not five fixed speeds or a requirement that every object follow one rhythm. Minutes, rounds, quarters, deliberation cycles, and years are merely typical examples; actual duration depends on evidence and task. [T-main]

The immediate type includes emotions, attention, bodily arousal, and local prices, triggered by signal arrival or shocks; short fluctuations cannot directly become long-term changes. The interactional type concerns trust, strategies, relational expectations, and local norms, advancing through multiple action–feedback rounds. Equal total counts may yield different results with different sequences and memories; each interaction cannot be treated as an independent, identically distributed reset. [T-main]

Organizational roles, budgets, processes, and indicators advance through decisions, execution, and review; a decision is not implementation. Institutional rules, rights, responsibilities, appeals, and records require checking actual procedural changes, write-back, and execution. Verbal promises are insufficient, and authorization and legal validity require separate recording. A procedure being carried out does not automatically establish valid authorization; ‘the institutional clock has arrived’ cannot generate authority. [T-main]

Long-term capability, identity, infrastructure, culture, and intergenerational change involve accumulation, learning, maintenance, and replacement. Short-term observations cannot guarantee lasting change, but classifying an object as long-term also does not establish that it cannot change today. Some long-term accumulation may become visible at thresholds, requiring specific dynamic grounds. [T-main]

The source separates two kinds of updating: external events directly update only variables reached through channels under satisfied conditions; endogenous processes, expiration, accumulation, and recovery advance according to their own clocks and the rules already stated. Unreached does not mean unchanged. Without new grounds, retain the last observed value with its time and uncertainty, or mark unknown, rather than marking an old value with today's time. An observation becoming stale changes knowledge status, not necessarily the entity for better or worse. [T-main]

The financial passage shows how asynchrony changes effects: prices may change before credit limits await revaluation or renewal; fixed- and floating-rate contracts adjust payments differently; public guarantees may first relieve cash shortfalls and later allocate losses. Compare when constraints become effective, alternative financing arrives, recovery occurs, and irreversible harm arises, not just final amounts. Prolonged short-term support is not restored long-term solvency. [T-main；T-finance]

This section's additional Cash and Counseling observation is that variables in the same nine-month interview do not share one observation window: care use looks back two weeks, while equipment and modifications cover nine months since enrollment. Different allowance start dates further mean that a nine-month observation date does not imply nine months of intervention for everyone. The report's short-term limitations also prevent interpreting that satisfaction measurement as a lasting institutional effect. This supports window discipline, not empirical exhaustiveness of the five clock categories. [P-CC]

The strongest objection is that multi-clock states are difficult to maintain. Begin with explicit expiration dates, actual records, and necessary validity-period management, refining only when the task depends on finer dynamics. Without dynamic estimates, do not draw smooth decay curves. For indeterminate variables, retain the last observation and an unknown current value rather than generate a complete but false real-time snapshot. [T-main；T-snapshot]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    For each variable, list updating triggers, time units, observation time, lookback window, and validity period.

  2. 2

    First check the event's direct channels, then concurrent endogenous, expiration, accumulation, or recovery processes.

  3. 3

    Tie each update to grounds; unreached variables neither reset automatically nor are automatically assumed constant.

  4. 4

    Compare constraint activation, alternative resources, and harm windows, distinguishing short-term support from long-term recovery.

  5. 5

    Retain historical values and uncertainty in stale records; mark the current value unknown without current grounds.

Distinctions to keep clear

Process clock

The rules by which actual states change.

≠

Observation window

The period covered by evidence; it cannot replace process speed.

Decision

A plan is proposed or approved through the relevant procedure.

≠

Implementation

Resources, processes, or actions have actually occurred.

Unaffected by this event

No direct channel from this event exists.

≠

Unchanged in reality

Also requires ruling out endogenous processes, expiration, and other effects.

Historical observation

A value grounded at that time.

≠

Current value

Requires sufficient timeliness and updating grounds.

Teaching construction: prices change first, contracts update laterTeaching scenario

AssumptionsEntirely constructed, single currency, no fees; revaluation and effective dates and permission to repay are stipulated.

Suppose a constructed collateralized loan has balance 50 yuan and is revalued at 60% of month-end market value, initially 100 yuan. On day 1, price falls to 80, but the contract keeps the old limit of 60 through day 30. Day-30 revaluation sets the limit to 48, yielding a contractual shortfall of 2 if the balance remains 50. If alternative cash of 2 arrives on day 10 and is repaid on day 29, the balance becomes 48, so there is no such shortfall on day 30. If cash arrives only on day 31, day-30 consequences depend on contractual grace provisions. The day-1 price shock is not equivalent to a margin call that day.

BoundaryNo actual contracts or default behavior were measured; price feedback and long-term solvency are not inferred.

Teaching construction: expiration can occur without new eventsTeaching scenario

AssumptionsConstant battery consumption is a constructed rule, not measured equipment data; the trust example has no numerical scale.

A constructed device has 10 battery units today and a stated consumption rule of 1 unit/hour without charging. Even without external messages for three hours, its battery becomes 7 under this deterministic model. Another variable, ‘member trust,’ has only last week's interview and no credible evolution rule; one cannot likewise subtract 3 or declare it still equal to last week's value. Retain the historical report and mark the current judgment unknown.

BoundaryThis distinguishes stated endogenous dynamics from unsupported imputation, without predicting real emotions.

A nine-month interview does not give every variable a nine-month windowDocumented case

The methods in the 2005 Cash and Counseling report separate human care over the preceding two weeks from equipment and modifications during nine months since enrollment; it also records some intervention-group members still not receiving allowances at interview.

10.8Joint State Snapshots ​

In briefA snapshot is like a state card with sources and times: it fixes projection's starting point and identifies unknown cells, preventing later events from being secretly written back into the beginning.

A snapshot is a fixed starting point for projection. It does not permanently reproduce reality. It must state the point in time at which the snapshot is taken, when the evidence cutoff falls, the actors and circles referred to, relation and membership mappings, the material state and the experience–meaning state, channels, constraints, the five kinds of clock, the scale profile, unknowns, residuals, and the identity criterion.

Each value in a snapshot should be marked with its status: observed, supported hypothesis, candidate, disputed, or one of the four missing-data states of §2.9. An observed value that cannot be settled because qualifying sources conflict with one another about the same object is recorded as “unknown,” with conflicting sources noted; “disputed” is used for inferred values and means that the evidence or explanations supporting the value conflict (§9.3). When sources conflict, first retain the respective values, how each was produced, and which version each came from. A combined estimate and its uncertainty may be listed separately only if there are grounds for both the measured object and the model used to combine results. An arithmetic mean cannot resolve the original conflict by itself. If a circle is internally differentiated, do not represent all positions with a single mean. If necessary, establish subcircles or use a distributional representation, but this requires going through object admission (§10.1) again.

10.8Note

Understanding this section

10.8 Joint-state snapshot

A snapshot is like a state card with sources and times: it fixes projection's starting point and identifies unknown cells, preventing later events from being secretly written back into the beginning.

The source calls a snapshot ‘a fixed starting point for projection’. What is fixed is one version of a representation and its evidence cutoff for a specified task, not reality itself. Snapshot time specifies the time being described; evidence cutoff determines which acquired materials may be used. Times of historical occurrence, record creation, and researcher access may differ. Later evidence should create a new version or correction record, not erase what was unknown in the old version. [T-main；T-clock]

Read this list by responsibility: the actors and circles referred to identify whom we discuss; relations and membership mappings specify who relates to whom and how; M/Ψ retain resources and experience; channels and constraints specify which changes can propagate; five clocks declare separate updating times; scale profiles prevent mixing axes into a size ranking; unknowns, residuals, and identity criteria identify unexplained aspects and whether the object remains the same across time. Complete items provide checkability, not completeness of reality. [T-main；T-joint]

Label each value separately as observed, supported hypothesis, candidate, disputed, or one of the four missing-data states of §2.9 (unknown, not applicable, unobservable, withheld for protection). Observed means a record through a specific channel, without guaranteeing no measurement error; a supported hypothesis has evidence and reasons but is still not direct observation; candidates await testing; disputed is used for inferred values and preserves the conflicting evidence or explanations and their grounds; an observed value that cannot be settled because qualifying sources conflict about the same object is recorded as unknown, with conflicting sources noted; unknown means insufficient basis for a current judgment; not applicable must follow the task's definition, not reluctance to address an item. These distinct statuses cannot be inserted into one numerical series as equally reliable measurements. [T-main]

For missing values, this section's status labels use the four missing-data states of §2.9 rather than a separate list: besides unknown and not applicable, they separate unobservable through the current channel/window and withheld for protection. An experiential item may be withheld for protection while supporting material exists; ‘no public value’ does not imply no experience or loss. Snapshots should retain necessary statuses without exposing specific private content. [T-missing]

When sources conflict, first retain values, generation methods, and versions side by side. If two records actually measure different objects, windows, or units, correct comparability first; if they measure the same quantity, a combination model is still required before listing an aggregate estimate and uncertainty separately. Arithmetic averaging can help under appropriate models but is no automatic arbiter. Original conflicts cannot be deleted merely because an intermediate number is generated. [T-main]

Internal differences cannot be represented only by circle means. Use distributions, quantiles, positional records, or subcircles with object grounds. A distribution representation need not add an entity; naming a subgroup an independent circle requires renewed admission for boundaries, roles, interfaces, windows, and identity. Neither labels nor means can invent individual facts. [T-main; T-entry]

This section adds comparison definitions from Cash and Counseling: the report defines “elderly” as 65 and over in two states but 60 and over in Florida, and excludes some proxy opinions under specified rules. Copying each state's elderly satisfaction rate into one snapshot would lose denominator differences. Record them without implying a calculation error or automatically prohibiting all model-based pooling. [P-CC]

The strongest objection is that snapshots, once fixed, become outdated. Retain observation time and validity duration in each version, choosing reobservation timing by task risk. Fixing them makes projection starting points traceable; updating prevents later judgments from expiring. If unknown key items could change conclusions, give only conditional paths or stop the affected strong judgments rather than filling values to make every item complete. [T-main; T-clock]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Specify snapshot time, material cutoff, task scope, and version, recording relevant times separately.

  2. 2

    Reference actors, circles, and relations, stating M/Ψ, constraints, clocks, scale, the evidence status, and the identity criterion.

  3. 3

    Label evidence status value by value; treat sensitive missingness under its protection status.

  4. 4

    Retain conflicting sources and generation processes, adding a combined estimate only with model support.

  5. 5

    Check internal differences and readmit new subobjects; create traceable new versions for updates.

Distinctions to keep clear

Snapshot time

The time the state is meant to represent.

≠

Evidence cutoff

The acquisition boundary for material allowed in this round.

Unknown

Insufficient grounds.

≠

Not applicable

Under the declared definition, this item does not answer this task.

Candidate value

An explanation or parameter awaiting testing.

≠

Observed value

A record through a particular channel, still potentially erroneous.

Distribution summary

Preserves multiple positions within an object.

≠

New subcircle

Proposes a new structural object requiring admission material.

Mathematical teaching construction: equal means, different positionsTeaching scenario

AssumptionsArtificial data with two distinct people; nontransferability applies only to the first task, and the 4-hour threshold is stipulated.

Two artificial groups have available work hours A=(0,10), B=(5,5), both averaging 5. If each person must perform at least 4 hours of nontransferable work, one person in A cannot, while both in B can. The mean answers total hours divided by headcount but not person-by-person feasibility. If work is freely transferable and only a joint 10 hours matters, the difference may no longer affect the answer.

BoundaryHours are not welfare or real group characteristics; sufficiency changes with the task.

Teaching construction: conflicting records and poolingTeaching scenario

AssumptionsCounts and model assumptions are artificial; no claim that actual devices satisfy them.

Two artificial counters report 10 and 14 items at the same time. First check counting boundaries, duplication, delays, and error rather than declaring 12 the truth. With additional assumptions that both counters are unbiased, independent, and equally variable, mean 12 can be an estimate under those assumptions; retain 10,14 and the model, with uncertainty explained. Because variance and repeat counts are unspecified, no confidence interval is calculated here.

BoundaryOpposes unsupported pooling, not supported statistical estimation.

The cross-state label “elderly” does not mean the same age definitionDocumented case

Note a to Table 5 in the 2005 report specifies elderly samples of 65 and over in Arkansas/New Jersey and 60 and over in Florida; Table 3 notes separately give proxy-response exclusions for some satisfaction and opinion questions.

If a value is recorded, may its measurement process be omitted?

No. Observation channel, object, window, and possible error still affect interpretation.

Basis: Value-specific evidential responsibility.

If two groups have the same mean, can both meet everyone's minimum needs?

Not necessarily. Distributions or positions are needed; means can hide local shortfalls.

Basis: The teaching work-hours example.

If material is withheld for protection, may it be recorded as nonexistent?

No. Preserve protection status and what may be disclosed; do not invent values.

Basis: §5.8 missing states.

10.9Boundary Perturbation and Object Conversion ​

In briefChange how the boundary is drawn and see whether the conclusion holds; then check whether the real object's structure changed. Analyst redrawing and actual object transformation need separate records.

Multi-circle models can easily mistake chosen boundaries for natural boundaries. At least three kinds of perturbation must be tested. Change the membership threshold and check whether the conclusion is stable. Move the time window and check whether the relation still holds. Replace or remove a circle and check whether the joint model’s gain disappears. If small changes in the boundary reverse the conclusion, narrow the conclusions that depend on that boundary and report the sensitivity; a grouping gain already claimed is recorded under §4.3 as “not supported or unresolved.”

If a circle’s identity criterion no longer holds after an event, object conversion or dissolution should be recorded. For example, a temporary rescue group may become a formal institution, a project team may split into competing alliances, a platform community may migrate to a new platform, or a household’s care arrangements may be reorganized after a member exits. A new object cannot overwrite the old object’s failures, responsibilities, or historical traces.

10.9Note

Understanding this section

10.9 Boundary perturbation and object conversion

Change how the boundary is drawn and see whether the conclusion holds; then check whether the real object's structure changed. Analyst redrawing and actual object transformation need separate records.

The source warns that models can “mistake chosen boundaries for natural boundaries.” Membership thresholds, observation times, and adjacent objects usually involve analytical choices requiring task and material grounds. Perturbation is not arbitrary selection for a preferred result; it changes choices within defensible ranges to reveal a conclusion's dependencies. Where an explicit legal or contractual boundary is required, surrounding sensitivity analysis remains possible, but another boundary cannot impersonate the original question. [T-main; T-entry]

The first perturbation changes membership thresholds, for example slightly raising participation frequency and tracing who leaves the denominator, which channels disappear, and whether the outcome changes. The second moves the time window, checking event-only relations or expired records. The third replaces or removes a circle, checking whether joint-model gain disappears or whether the circle merely duplicates another variable. These ask different questions; performing one does not establish comprehensive robustness. [T-main]

If slight, reasonable boundary changes reverse important conclusions, downgrade corresponding grouping-gain support and report sensitivity. Reversals may also reflect real thresholds or changed task definitions; they do not mechanically make all objects nonexistent. Explain where change occurs and which window/use is supported. Reduced explanatory or foresight gain cannot delete independently supported affected people, organizations, or responsibility relations. [T-main; T-entry; T-complex]

Object conversion instead means the original identity criterion no longer holds after an event. Source examples include formalizing a temporary rescue group, project splitting, platform migration, and care reorganization. Whether a genuinely new object exists depends on the original identity criterion: renaming need not change the object, and limited member turnover may remain within tolerance. Even without renaming, breaks in roles, interfaces, or continuity may require conversion or dissolution records. [T-main; T-entry]

Conversion records should retain the old object's identity and definition, break time, and grounds; create a new definition for the new object and specify inherited, changed, and unresolved connections. The new object cannot overwrite old failures, responsibilities, and historical traces. This preserves responsibility questions; it does not let the framework decide that every responsibility necessarily carries over or disappears. Legal, contractual, and actual responsibilities still need matter-specific verification. [T-main]

Cash and Counseling is reused here to show how boundary choices may change comparison objects: some opinion questions exclude paid-caregiver proxies, and the report explicitly notes unequal exclusion between groups, potentially biasing corresponding estimates. It warns that sample boundaries and original random-assignment groups are different sets. Without individual data, this lesson cannot claim completed perturbation analysis or an actual conclusion reversal. [P-CC]

The strongest objection is that sensitivity checks make every boundary endlessly suspect. Predeclare reasonable perturbation ranges, key outcomes, and stopping standards: changes beyond the task's definition become new questions, known irrelevant dimensions are not perturbed without limit, and decisive unchecked boundaries retain limitations. This preserves testability without equating lack of unconditional robustness with inability to make any bounded judgment. [T-main; T-complex]

When grouping gain disappears after boundary perturbation, downgrade the corresponding gain support and state applicable boundaries; independently supported organizations, relations, or responsibilities remain facts. A changed identity criterion also requires an independent object-conversion record; better prediction after redrawing cannot retroactively mean the old object never failed.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Preserve original boundaries, window, the object's identity criterion, and key conclusions.

  2. 2

    Within justified ranges, separately perturb membership thresholds, time windows, and circle sets.

  3. 3

    Trace changes in denominators, channels, and conclusions rather than reporting only the best result.

  4. 4

    Downgrade and qualify sensitive conclusions while retaining independently established object and responsibility facts.

  5. 5

    When the identity criterion no longer holds in reality, record conversion/dissolution; the new object's definition does not overwrite old records.

Distinctions to keep clear

Boundary perturbation

A definitional change in the analytical representation.

≠

Object conversion

A real event makes the stated identity conditions fail.

Unstable gain

A model's additional explanation for a task is unreliable.

≠

Object nonexistence

Requires different object material; it does not follow from the former.

New name

A changed label.

≠

New object

Judged through the identity criterion and structural material, not names alone.

Mathematical teaching construction: a small membership-threshold change reverses the conclusionTeaching scenario

AssumptionsEntirely artificial; scores are stipulated measurements and thresholds are assumed open to discussion here. No population extrapolation.

Three artificial members have participation scores 0.49,0.51,0.90 and proposal support coded 1 for yes, 0 for no, with records 0,0,1. Threshold ≥0.50 includes two people, support 1/2=50%; threshold ≥0.52 leaves one, support 1/1=100%. If the conclusion requires support strictly above 50%, it changes from failing to passing. Report denominator 2→1 together with threshold choice, rather than claiming the entire real group changed its opinion.

BoundaryShows boundary sensitivity, not the legality of actual decisions or unreliability of every membership threshold.

Teaching construction: preserving traceable history during migrationTeaching scenario

AssumptionsBoth identity criteria are artificial and predeclared, not changed afterward to suit preferences.

Artificial group C has an identity criterion requiring continued collaboration on a specified platform under the same management rules. If both platform interfaces and management rules change after migration and the old criterion is not met, archive C's state through migration day, create C2, and record personnel overlap, rule changes, and unresolved responsibilities. Under another task's identity criterion requiring only continued collaboration on a project, migration may not break that criterion.

BoundaryObject identity depends on the task's definition; legal allocation of old obligations is not adjudicated here.

Opinion-question exclusion rules change comparison setsDocumented case

To avoid interested proxy evaluations, the Cash and Counseling report did not ask proxies who were also paid caregivers some satisfaction and unmet-needs questions. Its limitations section notes more exclusion in the intervention group, potentially making the corresponding groups incomparable.
